bodyHTML:
Contributing guidelines

  • I have read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Module(s)

mini.ai

Question

Is is possible to make it work with attributes?

{
    "echasnovski/mini.ai",
    opts = function()
      local ai = require("mini.ai")
      return {
        custom_objects = {
          r = ai.gen_spec.treesitter({ a = "@attribute.outer", i = "@attribute.inner" }),
        },
      }
    end,
  }

This is essentially what I am passing at the moment to test this but doesn't seem to work for me.

Doing var(I can't figure out a good key to use for attributes as a is already used for arguments) should visual select className in this :

<div
 className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 bg-[#F3F3F3]"
>
</div>

comment_data.body:
If you are using tree-sitter for that (which is indeed a more robust way), you'd have to write own query with custom capture specifically for attribute name. The general workflow is roughly as follows: - Open a test file which has attached tree-sitter parser. Like 'test.html' with the `
` text you mentioned above. - Run `:InspectTree` and see if there are dedicated nodes for regions you want to select. In this particular case there is: `(attribute_name)`. - Inspect [html queries in 'nvim-treesitter-textobjects'](https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter-textobjects/blob/master/queries/html/textobjects.scm) to see if there is already something present there. Unfortunately, there isn't, which means you'd have to write own query file. - Create a file '~/.config/nvim/after/queries/html/textobjects.scm' and add the following lines: ```scm ;; extends (attribute_name) @attribute_name ``` - Use `@attribute_name` capture when defining custom 'mini.ai' tree-sitter based textobject. As this only makes sense for 'html' filetype, my suggestion would be to create a file '~/.config/nvim/after/ftplugin/html.lua' with the following content: ```lua if _G.MiniAi ~= nil then vim.b.miniai_config = { custom_textobjects = { r = _G.MiniAi.gen_spec.treesitter({ a = '@attribute_name', i = '@attribute_name' }), }, } end ``` This will make both `var` and `vir` work as to select any attribute names, but only inside html files. Hope this was helpful.
comment_data.bodyHTML:
If you are using tree-sitter for that (which is indeed a more robust way), you'd have to write own query with custom capture specifically for attribute name. The general workflow is roughly as follows:

  • Open a test file which has attached tree-sitter parser. Like 'test.html' with the <div className="..."></div> text you mentioned above.

  • Run :InspectTree and see if there are dedicated nodes for regions you want to select. In this particular case there is: (attribute_name).

  • Inspect html queries in 'nvim-treesitter-textobjects' to see if there is already something present there. Unfortunately, there isn't, which means you'd have to write own query file.

  • Create a file '~/.config/nvim/after/queries/html/textobjects.scm' and add the following lines:

    ;; extends
(attribute_name) @attribute_name

  • Use @attribute_name capture when defining custom 'mini.ai' tree-sitter based textobject. As this only makes sense for 'html' filetype, my suggestion would be to create a file '~/.config/nvim/after/ftplugin/html.lua' with the following content:

    if _G.MiniAi ~= nil then
  vim.b.miniai_config = {
    custom_textobjects = {
      r = _G.MiniAi.gen_spec.treesitter({ a = '@attribute_name', i = '@attribute_name' }),
    },
  }
end

    This will make both var and vir work as to select any attribute names, but only inside html files.

Hope this was helpful.
